text:
In Al-Adsani v. the United Kingdom (Grand Chamber, 21 November 2001), the European Court of Human Rights held that the United Kingdom did not breach the Convention by upholding Kuwait’s state immunity and refusing Al-Adsani’s civil claim for damages for alleged torture. It found no violation of Article 3 unanimously, and no violation of Article 6 § 1 by nine votes to eight, treating the immunity bar as a proportionate limit on access to court under a generally recognised rule of international law.
